notes: Documented regulator actions over hard-to-cancel subscriptions — the 'hidden unsubscribe / roach motel' pattern that a single page view cannot show.

Brief §11: no unverified brand-level claims. Only legal actions by a regulator belong here, worded as what was alleged, with the agency, case and date. Never a review site, a forum, or NightWatch's own detections.
Shown in the popup as background about the company, separately from what was detected on the page, and never counted in the badge.
Bundled with the extension: nothing is looked up online (brief §4). Before relying on an entry in the report, check it against the regulator's own announcement and add its URL to 'source'.

records.summary: In 2023 the US Federal Trade Commission sued Amazon, alleging it signed people up to Prime without clear consent and made cancelling deliberately difficult through a multi-step process. Amazon settled the case in 2025.
records.source: US Federal Trade Commission, FTC v. Amazon.com, Inc. (filed June 2023; settled September 2025)

records.summary: In 2024 the US Department of Justice, referred by the Federal Trade Commission, sued Adobe, alleging it hid an early termination fee and made subscriptions hard to cancel.
records.source: US Department of Justice on behalf of the FTC, United States v. Adobe Inc. (filed June 2024)

records.summary: In 2025 the US Federal Trade Commission sued Uber, alleging it charged people for Uber One without consent and made the subscription hard to cancel.
records.source: US Federal Trade Commission, FTC v. Uber Technologies, Inc. (filed April 2025)
